contents.entry: Pointers: parent, siblings, schema, shared volumes
Input: the tick:scheduler entity and lease.granted
Output record: dispatch, and the sched:tick entity
Mechanism: the level-triggered tick in the Go service
How it starts without an agent typing
Every wait, its timeout and its fallback
Retries: three attempts, then recover and report
Many agents at once: the collision answer
State paths written and the cleanup script for each

pointers.shared: Where this node goes live in the one cut-over order of the book

purpose.sentence: On every scheduler tick the Go service compares the work that should be running with the work that is running, and writes one dispatch record for each gap, so that no agent and no human ever starts a seat.
purpose.is: The one place a seat run or a code job is born: a dispatch record is the only thing N-13, N-14 and N-15 consume to bring a seat up.
Level-triggered: a lost record never strands a ticket, because the next tick sees the gap again; a duplicate record never double-dispatches, because the dispatch key is deterministic.
purpose.is-not: Not a router of records by table: the old belt routed every record through factory/config/routes.json; here records are facts in the store and the tick derives the plan from the facts.
Not a seat, not a pane, not a prompt: dispatch is a row the launcher reads, never text typed into a window.
purpose.decisions: D01 (Go service with gRPC owns scheduling), D02 (one-shot seats), D11 (code does mechanical jobs), D17 (stall timer replaces the idle alarm), T02 and T03 (Symphony loop, level-triggered reconcile), V02 (claim before act).

record.field: A counter that only grows; the tick that starts this traversal.
UTC second of the tick.
The configured interval, default 5 (config key tick.scheduler_seconds, N-06 schedule; the old belt's factory/config/runner.json poll_seconds 10 is the source of the shape).
record.note: Ticks are entities, not log records: N-06 compare-and-swap writes the entity tick:scheduler and broadcasts it on an in-process channel with a buffer of 1, so a slow tick coalesces (N-06 output rule); this node consumes that channel.

record.field: The lease key: ticket, phase and attempt (N-02 lease_key).
The work order id the lease is about.

One of worker, reviewer, spec (a cut request, key CR-<request id>, nodes/N-03/spec.xml#input) or gate; the phase of the traversal the lease grants. The validator is never dispatched: N-18 is code that validates every draft on its own tick.
1 to 3, the attempt this lease grants (from N-02, or from N-11 on a re-entry).
The role N-02 copied from the ticket's phase.
Empty until N-07 dispatches; then the dispatch id (N-02: a string the store does not interpret).
The fencing token: a store-wide counter that only grows; every later write about this run carries it (N-02 output).
Incremented by N-02 on every grant, renewal or revoke; the compare-and-swap version of the lease row.
UTC second the lease dies without a renewal (N-12 reads it).
The renewal interval N-15 must keep: config key lease.heartbeat_seconds, default 30 (shared/state-store.xml#config-keys).
record.join: The lease body carries no backoff; N-07 joins the attempt record of N-11 by the same key (ticket:phase:attempt) and reads its not_before; a lease with no attempt record (attempt 1) has none.

input.reads: The tick also reads, without consuming: the set of open dispatch records with no terminal seat.result, the heartbeat age per run (N-12 owns the verdict, N-07 only counts live runs), the caps table, the roles table, the build-mode state (N-44), the entity flag:hold (set by N-29 from a control.action or a card, read into memory on every scheduler tick per N-06), and the halt record (503).
input.starts-when: The tick:scheduler entity is broadcast and the service holds the leader lease node:N-07:leader (see many-agents).

record.field: The record id.
ticket, colon, phase, colon, attempt; a second write with the same key is refused by N-01 with 409 and read as already dispatched.
The work order id.
worker, reviewer, spec-author (for phase spec), or the code role gate; the role file N-13 renders from (shared/seat-contract.xml#roles).
The lease phase, copied.
The lease attempt, copied.
UTC second by which the run must end: at plus the role's run_deadline_seconds (default worker 3600, reviewer 1800, spec-author 3600, gate 60; source Symphony turn_timeout_ms 3600000, I02 section 6).
The lease key and its fencing token, copied; every heartbeat and the seat.result carry the token.
Absolute path under the state root of the brief N-13 renders, named by ticket, phase and attempt; written before the dispatch record (see mechanism step 6).
build, verify or system; from the ticket's epic (three loops, AGENTS.md Law: three loops, always).
Copied from the lease; always at or before at.
role-unknown, brief-missing, files-claimed, or address-unknown: the address check failed before any dispatch.
The ticket held.
desired, live, dispatched, held_by_cap, held_by_hold, refused, conflicts_409; the counters the Stats screen reads.
The tick this closes.
record.note: An entity, not a log record: compare-and-swap written every tick (version grows) and pushed by N-31; 17,280 scheduler ticks a day in the records log would bury every real record (N-06 output rule). A tick that found a gap also leaves its dispatch records, which are the log.

output.ends-when: Every gap of this tick has a dispatch, a dispatch.refused or a hold reason, and the sched:tick entity is written; the traversal is over and the next tick is a new traversal.

mechanism.where: Go package sched inside the one service binary (D01, D09); it keeps the core interfaces Clock, JobStore and Ledger of scheduler/internal/core/interfaces.go and the fake clock of scheduler/internal/testkit, and drops the routes table (rejected, see rejected item 1).
mechanism.shape: One goroutine runs ticks; it never blocks on a dispatch, because a dispatch is a store write and nothing else (SPEC-16 overview sh-loop: ticks never block on a job). The tick function is pure over a snapshot: Tick(snapshot, now, config) returns intents; the engine writes intents with compare-and-swap.
mechanism.step: Read the leader lease node:N-07:leader from N-02. Not held by this process: write nothing, log one line, end the tick. Held: continue with its fencing token.

Read the halt record and the entity flag:hold. Halt (503) present: end the tick after writing sched:tick with held_by_hold equal to desired. Hold present: dispatch nothing new but still count, so the Stats screen shows the backlog.

Take one snapshot from N-01 in a single read transaction: leases with empty holder and not_before at or before now; open dispatch records (no seat.result, no stall record with the same lease_token); the caps table; the roles table; the build-mode state; the file claims of in-flight tickets.

Desired set equals the leases of step 3 (worker and reviewer leases on tickets, spec leases on cut-request keys CR-..., which dispatch as role spec-author with the request as the brief target, and gate leases) ordered by lane priority (system first, then verify, then build; source memory three-loops-always), then ticket priority, then lease at. Live set equals the open dispatch records. Gap equals desired minus the tickets with a live run in the same phase.

Clip the gap to capacity: total live seats below caps.max_seats (default 16; owner card C27 lever 2, L06 section 5.8 item g), per role below the role's max_seats, and two worker slots reserved for the system lane (memory three-loops-always). A lease clipped by a cap is held with reason cap and counted; it is not refused and no record is written for it, because the next tick sees it again (SPEC-16.C c-caps: hold, never refuse).

Address check before any dispatch (D01 B; Symphony SPEC.md reconcile before dispatch): the role exists in the roles table; the brief renders (N-13 is asked synchronously over the in-process interface to render the brief for ticket, phase, attempt, and returns a path); the ticket's declared files overlap no other in-flight ticket (V07; N-14 refuses again at start). A failed check writes dispatch.refused 412 with the reason and ends this lease's traversal; N-11 decides the retry.

Write the dispatch record with idempotency_key ticket:phase:attempt and the lease token, and in the same transaction compare-and-swap the lease row: holder from empty to the dispatch id, expected generation from step 3. A 409 on either write means another tick already dispatched it; read it back and count it as live.

A dispatch whose role is a code role (gate) is not a seat: the service performs it in process at once, by writing the record the role names (gate: a pr.opened record with the same head sha and attempt n plus 1 for N-23), then writes seat.result done 200 for the dispatch so the run is terminal. No pane is opened.
Compare-and-swap write the sched:tick entity with the counters. End. The next tick:scheduler broadcast starts a new traversal.
mechanism.invariant: A ticket and phase has at most one live dispatch at any time: guaranteed by the idempotency key (one per attempt) and the lease holder compare-and-swap (one attempt granted at a time by N-02).
Every dispatch names a lease that exists and is unexpired at write time; N-12 kills the run if the lease later dies.
mechanism.diagram: flowchart TD T["tick:scheduler entity"] --> L{"leader lease node:N-07:leader held?"} L -- no --> E["log one line, end"] L -- yes --> F{"halt 503?"} F -- yes --> D9["sched:tick entity, end"] F -- no --> S["snapshot: leases, open dispatches, caps, roles, claims"] S --> G["gap = desired minus live, ordered by lane then priority then age"] G --> C["clip to caps and reserved system slots"] C --> A{"address check: role, brief, files"} A -- fails --> R["dispatch.refused 412 to N-11"] A -- passes --> W["write dispatch + CAS lease holder"] W -- 409 --> V["already dispatched, count as live"] W -- ok --> K{"code role?"} K -- yes --> P["perform in process, seat.result 200"] K -- no --> N13["N-13, N-14, N-15 bring the seat up"] P --> D9 N13 --> D9 V --> D9 R --> D9

start.sentence: Nothing here starts by an agent typing.
start.by: The systemd user unit of the Go service (N-06, unit.start) starts the tick goroutine; N-06 writes the tick:scheduler entity every tick.scheduler_seconds (5) from its own clock and broadcasts it in process; every broadcast is this node's input.
start.restart: After a crash the service restarts under its unit (Restart on failure, start limit 3 in the interval; SPEC-17 1.1.0 draft s-supervision U1) and the first tick re-reads the store: dispatch records with no seat.result are live, leases with empty holder are desired, and nothing is remembered in memory (Symphony SPEC.md restart recovery, I02 section 5 and 4.4).
start.never: No make target, no pane, no prompt and no herdr call starts a tick (D08).

wait.fallback: end the tick with sched:tick snapshot_ok false; after three ticks in a row, write store.unreachable 500 to N-28 once (latched by the first failed tick n) and keep ticking
treat as not held; write nothing; the next tick tries again
dispatch.refused 412 reason brief-missing; N-11 retries the lease on its backoff

wait.on: N-01 dispatch write plus lease CAS
wait.fallback: retry the write three times with 1 s, 2 s, 4 s between; then the lease is left unheld and the next tick sees it again; a 500 dispatch.write.failed record is written once per lease key
N-06 reports tick.missed 500 for the subkind and lists it in health (N-06 owns this bound); this node never sleeps or polls on its own

waits.rule: Every wait is a context deadline in Go; no time.Sleep exists in the tick path (SPEC-16 overview l-pure; L14 section 4.1).

retries.rule: Every automated step retries up to 3 times, then recovers and reports (global rule; plan principles.xml no-cog; failure-cases.xml crash).

step.name: store read
step.then: store.unreachable 500 once to N-28; ticking continues

step.name: dispatch write
step.then: dispatch.write.failed 500 once per lease; the lease stays unheld; the next tick retries

step.name: brief render
step.attempts: 1 per tick, 3 leases attempts via N-11
step.then: dead record by N-11 after attempt 3

retries.not-retried: A dispatch.refused for files-claimed is not retried by this node; the claim clears when the other ticket merges (N-09 merge record releases claims in N-45) and the next tick sees the lease again without an attempt spent, because no dispatch was written.
retries.report: Every then clause is a record in N-01 with code 500 and a kind in status-codes; N-28 builds exactly one card per latched kind and ticket.

many-agents.readers: Twenty seats can read this volume at once; it is one file with stable anchors and nothing in it changes at run time.
many-agents.one-scheduler: Exactly one tick goroutine dispatches at a time: the service takes the scheduler leader lease node:N-07:leader from N-02 (shared/state-store.xml#table-leases: ttl lease.leader_ttl_seconds 30, renewed every 10 s, fencing token; nodes/N-02/spec.xml#mechanism system-leases); the flock of N-06 already refuses a second service process, and this lease covers the hand-over between a stopping and a starting one; a second service process, started by hand or by a unit restart overlapping a slow stop, finds the lease held and ticks without writing. When the old process dies the lease expires and the new one takes it within one lease length.
many-agents.two-dispatches: Two ticks that both see the same gap (a leader change mid-tick) both try to write dispatch ticket:phase:attempt; N-01 refuses the second with 409 on the idempotency key, and the lease compare-and-swap refuses the second holder on generation; the loser reads the winner's record and counts it live. No seat is ever started twice for one attempt.
many-agents.launcher-claims: Many N-15 launchers may read dispatch records at once; a launcher claims a dispatch by compare-and-swap on its claimed_by field with the dispatch's lease_token, so one dispatch starts one run (N-15 volume owns that CAS; this volume only guarantees the key is unique).
many-agents.stale-writer: A seat whose lease was revoked by N-12 may still post a result with the old token; N-01 refuses any write whose lease_token is below the lease's current token with 409 stale-token (N-02 lease_stale), and this node never counts such a run as live.
many-agents.append-only: Dispatch records are never edited; a dispatch ends only by a seat.result or a stall record that names its lease_token.
many-agents.conflict-reports: Every 409 this node meets is logged with the key and counted in sched:tick conflicts_409; it is never a silent overwrite.
many-agents.test: Test case two-ticks-one-gap: two Tick calls over the same snapshot with a fake clock write exactly one dispatch and one 409 (checklist item c-two-ticks).

emits.acts: N-13, N-14, N-15 bring the seat up or the service performs the code role
N-40 Stats screen through N-31; nobody else
N-28 one card per lease key; N-41 alerts

reads.acts: this node dispatches nothing while it exists
not written by this node; the counter held_by_cap replaces the old 429 refusal records (SPEC-17 s-codes 429), because a hold is re-examined every tick and needs no record

state-paths.root: $COQ_STATE, default ${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/coq/coq-jev-herdr-plugin (AGENTS.md Law: runtime data never lives in git; bin/state-root.sh). The path elements below are in the form N-45's generator reads (rebuild/design/bin/registry.py over every state-paths element; ../N-45/spec.xml#state-paths), so every path has a cleanup entry.
state-paths.path: Rows in tables records, leases and dispatch, written only through N-01; retention is N-01's row (30 days default, roadmap defaults).

path.retention: P30D after the ticket's verified record

state-paths.path: Briefs N-13 renders at N-07's request, named by ticket, phase and attempt; dry-run listing first (N-45).
One JSON line per decision; rotated daily.

path.retention: P0D when the unit is inactive

state-paths.path: Touched every tick by the tick loop (SPEC-16.F f-belt-touch); overwritten on start.
state-paths.never: No path under the repository, no file in a worktree, no pane.

schema.defs: dispatch, dispatch_refused, tick_done (the sched:tick entity); tick and lease are references to ../N-06/record.schema.json#/$defs/tick and ../N-02/record.schema.json#/$defs/lease_granted; every record extends base (id, at, code, kind, node, ticket, attempt, seq, idempotency_key), the shape ../../shared/state-store.xml#table-records owns.

permissions.process: The Go service user unit; subscription auth is not involved (no LLM here, D11).
permissions.reads: N-01 store (read), N-02 leases (read and CAS on holder), roles table, caps table, build-mode state, halt and hold records.
permissions.writes: dispatch, dispatch.refused, store.unreachable, dispatch.write.failed records; the sched:tick entity; the briefs path by asking N-13; the scheduler log and heartbeat file.
permissions.never: No GitHub call, no git command, no herdr call, no pane, no prompt, no edit of any record, no file under the repository.
permissions.seat: No seat has permission to write dispatch records; N-01 refuses a dispatch whose writer is not the service (writer identity from the unix socket peer, D01).

lamp.name: scheduler
lamp.green: the sched:tick entity younger than 2 intervals and leader true
lamp.red: older, or store.unreachable open, or tick.missed for subkind scheduler

alert.to: N-41 and one card by N-28
N-41 and one card by N-28

monitoring.health: gRPC Health of the service reports sched: ok when the sched:tick entity is fresh; the probe is code, never an opinion (V08).

runbook.bring-up: Install the service unit (N-06); set sched.enabled true in the service config; the next tick dispatches. Proof: the sched:tick entity with n greater than 0 and leader true.
runbook.read-status: grpc Scheduler.Status on the control socket (scheduler.proto) prints desired, live, held, refused and the last tick from the sched:tick entity; the Machine screen (N-39) shows the same.
runbook.drain: grpc Scheduler.Drain: the leader keeps ticking, dispatches nothing new, counts live runs down to zero; resume by Reload.
runbook.hold: The owner holds the line from the Controls screen (N-42), which N-29 records as a ruling that sets the entity flag:hold; no command on this node.
runbook.recover-crash: Nothing to do: the unit restarts the service, the first tick re-reads the store (start section).
runbook.recover-store-unreachable: N-01 runbook; this node keeps ticking and clears its latch on the first good snapshot.

cleanup.mode: dry-run first, then --apply; three attempts then a cleanup.run 500 record (N-45)
removes the heartbeat file only when the unit is inactive

runbook.registry: All three entries are generated into shared/cleanup-registry.json by rebuild/design/bin/registry.py from the state-paths element above (../N-45/spec.xml#state-paths).

item.source: factory/config/routes.json; specs/scheduler/SPEC-16.B-routing.xml (design branch origin/feat/go-scheduler-design-one-xml-spec-per-domain-unde, not in this worktree)
item.reason: a routes table maps one record to one wake, which is edge-triggered: a lost or duplicated record is lost or doubled (K08, RC2). The tick derives the plan from the whole state every time (T03). The SDLC edges of the table survive as the phase order worker, reviewer, merge in dag.md section 4.

item.source: specs/scheduler/SPEC-16.D-jobs-retries-confirmation.xml#d-confirm (design branch origin/feat/go-scheduler-design-one-xml-spec-per-domain-unde, not in this worktree); scheduler.proto WakeCounters
item.reason: wake confirmation existed because a wake was text typed into a pane that might be busy or absent (RC2, RC4). A dispatch is a store row a launcher claims by compare-and-swap, so there is nothing to confirm; a run that never starts is caught by N-12 as a missing first heartbeat.

a refusal record per capacity miss produced one record a minute while a cap held (route-retry breadcrumb cwzvb). A cap hold is a counter re-examined every tick; the code 429 stays in the shared map for N-15's own refusals.

Make supplies order and idempotence for the owner's hand entry points and may wrap this service's control calls, but the dispatch decision lives in the Go service (D01 ruled Go with gRPC after T15 was written); a Make target that dispatched would be a second scheduler.
